question.text: Malabar Growth Fund (Category II AIF) seeks SEBI prior approval to invest USD 50 million in an offshore technology venture. Under SEBI's guidelines on overseas investment by AIFs/VCFs, which of the following limits apply?

answer.text: Overall cumulative cap of USD 1,500 million across all AIFs, first-come-first-served; the AIF's own overseas allocation cannot exceed 25% of its investable funds
No overall cap; AIF may invest up to 100% of corpus overseas
Each AIF can invest up to USD 500 million on its own; no SEBI approval needed
Only Category III AIFs may invest overseas; Cat II cannot

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular CIR/IMD/DF/7/2015 (as updated, including enhancement from USD 750 mn to USD 1,500 mn vide May 21, 2021 circular): (a) overall cumulative cap of USD 1,500 million for all AIFs/VCFs taken together, allocated first-come-first-served; (b) each AIF's overseas investment shall not exceed 25% of its own investable funds; (c) SEBI prior approval needed, valid for 6 months to complete investment; (d) investments must be in Cat-VI MMoU signatory jurisdictions with Indian connection; (e) cannot be in FATF high-risk countries. IFSC-domiciled Cat I/II are exempt from these limits. The Trap: Option B invents 'no cap'. Option C bypasses SEBI approval. Option D incorrectly excludes Cat II. The 25%-of-investable-funds cap is often forgotten. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests overseas-investment limits. FEMA Overseas Investment Regulations, 2022 are cross-tested in XXIV and X-A/B. FVCI route (different from AIF overseas route) is also tested in XIX-C. Manager's Pro-Tip: Track the USD 1.5 bn cap utilisation via SEBI's periodic updates on aifreporting@sebi.gov.in mailbox. File your overseas-investment proposal early in the fund's life — the first-come-first-served allocation regularly exhausts. If your approval lapses after 6 months unutilised, SEBI reallocates to waiting applicants.
